content:
This week, Apple continues to steadily expand its Apple Sports app, broadening its football coverage while also giving tennis fans a new way to follow some of the sport's biggest events. Here's what's new.

Apple Sports adds more football leagues and tennis schedules

When Apple first launched the Apple Sports app, the experience was fairly limited in terms of both availability and the actual sports covered.

Since then, the app has grown on both fronts, expanding to over 170 countries and regions while continuing to add support for new sports, leagues, and events.

For example, Apple Sports rolled out to 90 new countries earlier this year, with a slate of features built around the FIFA World Cup.

This week, Apple Sports rolled out a single update that brings the Australian A-League Men, Egyptian Premier League, Israeli Premier League, and South African Premier League into its football lineup.

In addition, Apple says the app now lets tennis fans "follow draws in real time... including brackets for Grand Slams and 1000-level events," and that users can "see the full list and results for each round at a glance."

Here's the full release notes for Apple Sports 4.4:

The football lineup keeps growing, with the addition of the Australian A-League Men, Egyptian Premier League, Israeli Premier League, and South African Premier League. Tennis fans can now follow draws in real time within Apple Sports, including brackets for Grand Slams and 1000-level events. See the full matchups and results for each round at a glance.

Are you using Apple Sports? Let us know in the comments.
